CHA.note: Boswell (knee) is out for Wednesday's season opener against the Nets.

BKN.note: Bilodeau (shoulder) has been ruled out for Saturday's game in Cleveland.

PHI.note: Barlow will miss at least the next two weeks of action due to a lumbar spine bone stress response, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
Fall (quadriceps) is out for Saturday's game against the Bucks.
Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN.

CHI.note: Claxton (hamstring) will be re-evaluated in two weeks, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.

WSH.note: The Wizards announced Thursday that Vukcevic (hip) will be re-evaluated in four weeks.
The Wizards announced Thursday that Watkins has undergone surgery for a torn ACL.

DAL.note: Head coach Dusty May said Flagg (shoulder) will be evaluated in the next couple of days, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
Lively (foot) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Pacers.

SA.note: Quaintance has been around the team but has not yet been cleared for basketball activities, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.

ATL.note: Gueye underwent surgery Tuesday to repair a fractured left foot that he suffered during a workout last week, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
Veesaar was diagnosed with a torn right ACL and is expected to miss the 2026-27 season, the Hawks announced Monday.

DEN.note: Johnson (ankle) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against New Orleans.
Jones (hamstring) is out for Saturday's game against the Pelicans.
Strawther (knee) was diagnosed with a left knee sprain Friday and will be re-evaluated in six weeks, Vinny Benedetto of The Denver Gazette reports.

PHX.note: Williams underwent surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss an extended period of time, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.

GS.note: Butler (knee) could return sometime between January and February as he continues recovering from a torn right ACL, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
Moody (knee) is progressing toward a potential return between December and January after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
Podziemski (back) told reporters Friday that he will not play in the second leg of the Warriors' back-to-back set Saturday against the Suns, Nick Friedell of The Athletic reports.
Porzingis is contemplating his future in basketball as he deals with recurring symptoms from the autoimmune condition termed as postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
